# Design — executive status notebook, 13 August 2026

**Deliverable:** `analysis-output/E_macro_pillar_worth_2026-08-13.ipynb`, generated by
`scripts/build_status_notebook.py`, plus doc-sync edits to `docs/pillar_status.md`
and `docs/PROJECT_GOAL.md`.

## Purpose and audience

A **progress artifact, not a decision artifact.** It reports what the project has
done and what it now knows; it does not ask for the go/no-go. That decision is
the stage outcome and comes later.

- **Room:** Max's boss (commissioning side) plus their leadership, together.
  Boss has full context; the leadership above them does not. Written for the
  person who does not, without patronising the one who does.
- **Posture:** supportive room, not a hostile one — optimise for clarity over
  persuasion. One attendee is technical and will push back, most likely on
  whether public ACS proxies mean anything.
- **Delivery:** presented live, notebook on screen, ~45–60 minutes.
- **Depth:** numbers in the body, methods in an appendix.
- **Constraints:** the public-data-only scope is already known to the room; one
  line of reference is enough.

## Framing

Titled by the finding, not the date: **"What each pillar is actually worth."**

Baseline for "progress" is the last update the room saw — the 6 August weekly
brief. The increment is 7–12 August: Source D partner-concentration indices
re-derived at market grain, three Source A experiments that all returned
negative, schema freeze on B/C/D/F, the drop-one test that scored every pillar,
Source F vindicated, Source A raised as the new open item.

The controlling idea: **prior rounds measured whether pillars correlate with each
other; this round measures what each one adds.** Coherence is not usefulness.

## Structure

Six body sections plus an appendix, ~30 cells.

### 0. Title and frame

One line on the public-data-only scope, one line on what changed since 6 August,
one line naming the controlling idea above.

### 1. The turn — from correlation to contribution (~5 min)

- Prior updates measured pillar-versus-pillar correlation, which measures
  coherence and redundancy rather than usefulness.
- New instrument: drop-one marginal R² against five external ACS targets, scored
  out-of-fold on states the model never trained on.
- The pre-registered decision rule, quoted, with the point that it was written
  before the numbers arrived.

### 2. The headline (~8 min)

- Per-pillar contribution figure with the shuffled-feature noise floor drawn on
  it as an annotated rule.
- The six-row table: pillar, contribution, positive-on-N, above-floor-on-N,
  verdict.
- The matrix as a whole beats a county-size baseline by +0.190 mean R², positive
  on all five targets. **Section 2 only — not promoted to the title.** The
  per-pillar table is the honest unit of analysis; +0.190 is context for it.
- The public-proxy caveat lands here, beside the headline, not deferred to the
  limitations section.

### 3. Two pillars moved (~10 min)

**Source F.** Failed the pairwise hub test (r = 0.495 raw against Source D
tonnage, −0.057 size-controlled) and passed the residual-variance test that
`pillar_status.md` itself proposed (+0.0413, second of six, positive 5 of 5,
above the noise floor 5 of 5). Both facts travel together. The internal arm's
+0.0510 raw is shown beside its +0.0063 ablated — roughly seven eighths of the
internal figure is USDA restating BLS.

**Source A.** −0.0000 marginal, positive on 2 of 5, above the floor on 2 of 5;
the only block negative in both arms. Shown per-target against the placebo band
to establish redundant-rather-than-broken: contributions run −0.0032 to +0.0070,
not wildly negative.

Closes on the conditional cut, **put to the room as an open question**:
recommend cutting A *unless* the consumer's real target rewards what A encodes
(named industries, universities, ports, protected land) — which only the
commissioning side can answer. The three counter-arguments from
`pillar-marginal-findings.md` §7 are presented alongside, not suppressed: A is
nearly free, the ACS targets are a poor match for what A encodes, and redundancy
inside a feature store is insurance rather than waste.

### 4. What was ruled out (~5 min, compressed)

- Three Source A experiments, all negative: section-scope whitelist, 384-d
  encoder, inverted tier rule. One figure, three lines of text.
- Source D partner-concentration indices re-derived at market grain; external
  mean lift moved +0.106 → +0.099.

Negative results are work, and in a justify-time-spent meeting what was ruled
out is part of the point — but it gets one compressed panel, not a section each.

### 5. What this still cannot answer (~4 min)

Deliberately trimmed. The room is supportive; eight minutes of caveats would be
over-correcting. Four items, tersely:

- **The fixed-effect objection.** If the consumer joins at DMA grain, a
  210-level dummy supplies everything a static DMA-keyed feature could. Shown
  with the grain chart: losing rows costs −0.122 mean lift, aggregating gains
  +0.099, and they roughly cancel.
- **No downstream label**, structurally — a consequence of the public-data-only
  scope, not an oversight.
- **Cross-sectional and single-period.** Temporal transfer is untested anywhere
  in this repo.
- **Sibling tiers.** `E_local` is at H3 res-8, `E_census` does not exist, and
  nobody owns the grain reconciliation. Flagged, not solved.

The consumer-facing grain-mismatch trap (effective n is the county count, so
random k-fold will flatter the feature in evaluation and do nothing in
production) moves to the appendix rather than the body.

### 6. Readiness panel (~5 min)

- What a go/no-go needs, against what exists today.
- Coverage, schema and vintage per pillar, read from `outputs/pillar_vintages.csv`
  — all six frozen.
- Remaining path expressed in weeks of availability, which is the binding
  constraint.

### Appendix (prose, jump-linked)

- **A1 — Do ACS proxies mean anything?** The hardest anticipated pushback gets
  its own subsection: what the proxies are, why they are the only non-circular
  evidence this project can produce, what an argument by analogy does and does
  not license, and what would settle it.
- **A2 — Method.** Drop-one design, ridge on an imputed design, GroupKFold on
  `state_fips`, the placebo construction behind the noise floor, and ablation of
  restatement columns.
- **A3 — Limitations**, carried over from `pillar-marginal-findings.md` §8
  without softening, including that B's and C's ordering is not settled at the
  placebo count used.
- **A4 — Per-pillar schema and null semantics**, with the grain-mismatch warning
  for the consuming team.
- **A5 — Artifact index.** Every figure names the script and CSV that produced
  it.

## Implementation

**Generator pattern.** `scripts/build_status_notebook.py` emits the notebook with
`nbformat`, following `scripts/build_weekly_brief.py`: code cells carry
`jupyter.source_hidden` and `collapsed` metadata so the notebook opens as a
document rather than as a program, and markdown cells carry the narrative.

**Data policy.** Every analysis script is re-run at build time —
`analyze_pillar_block_marginal`, `analyze_external_target`, `analyze_grain_effect`,
`analyze_pillar_matrix_signal`, `analyze_pillar_pair_crossvalidation`,
`analyze_feature_size_dependence` — and the notebook then reads the regenerated
`outputs/`. Nothing is hardcoded. Because seeds are fixed and `outputs/` is
git-tracked and clean before the run, `git diff outputs/` after the re-run is the
drift detector: any figure that moves is reported before the notebook is
presented, not discovered in the room.

**Charts.** Plotly, with a fresh design pass for a projector rather than a reuse
of the brief's screen-oriented figures: base type ≥16px, at most four series per
figure, direct labels in preference to legends, a single accent against neutral
grey, and the noise floor drawn as an annotated rule rather than a legend entry.
Balanced against tables — tables wherever the exact value is the point (pillar
contributions, coverage, vintages).

**Execution.** The notebook is executed at build time and committed executed, so
every output renders without anyone running a cell in the room.

## Wording constraints

`analysis-output/cross-source/pillar-marginal-findings.md` §9 carries a
forbidden-wording list that this notebook must satisfy:

- Not "Source F failed its test" — it failed the pairwise instrument and passed
  the residual-variance one; both halves travel together.
- Not "Source F is the second most important pillar" without "on five public ACS
  targets, measured as marginal R² over the rest of the matrix."
- F's internal +0.0510 never appears without +0.0063 beside it.
- Not "B and E are redundant" — they are complementary; B is individually weak.
- Not "Source A should be cut." The conditional, open-question framing chosen for
  section 3 satisfies this: the notebook states A's contribution, states the
  three reasons not to act, and puts the condition to the room.

## Doc sync

`docs/pillar_status.md` and `docs/PROJECT_GOAL.md` currently record "no cut
proposed" for Source A. Both are updated so the repo does not contradict the
notebook: A's status becomes a conditional open question dependent on the
consumer's real target, with the §7 counter-arguments preserved as the reasons
not to act unilaterally.

## Out of scope

- The five open questions for the commissioning side. They live in
  `docs/handoff_one_pager.md` and stay there; this notebook is pure progress.
- The go/no-go recommendation itself.
- The fusion step, which remains deliberately deferred.
- County choropleth maps — ~5MB per render and gitignored.
